question: What can I do with VA appointments online?
ground_truth: After signing in you can schedule and cancel some VA appointments, request approved community care appointments, review and print appointment lists and add them to a personal calendar, find the location of the facility, get after-visit summaries from some appointments, and review submitted travel pay claims.

question: Who can manage health appointments online?
ground_truth: Anyone registered as a patient in a VA health facility. Which appointments can be scheduled online depends on the facility, the type of health service and other factors.

question: Who should I contact if I have a question about scheduling an appointment?
ground_truth: Call your VA or community care health facility. The facility's phone number can be found with the VA facility locator.

question: Can I get a summary of my visit online?
ground_truth: Yes. After-visit summaries from some appointments are available online after signing in.

question: How do I refill my prescription online?
ground_truth: Sign in to the My HealtheVet experience on VA.gov, where you can refill and track your VA prescriptions.

question: Who is eligible to manage medications online?
ground_truth: Both must be true: you are enrolled in VA health care or another VA health benefits program and you have at least one prescription filled through a VA pharmacy.

question: Can I see my over-the-counter medicines and supplements in my VA records?
ground_truth: Yes. After signing in you can see a complete list of medications in your VA medical records, including over-the-counter medications, supplements and herbal remedies.

question: How can I get my meds refilled without calling anyone?
ground_truth: Use the online medication tools in My HealtheVet on VA.gov to refill and track VA prescriptions, if you are enrolled and fill at least one prescription through a VA pharmacy.

question: What do I need to have ready to apply for VA health care?
ground_truth: Social Security numbers for you, your spouse and dependents; military discharge papers (DD214) and service history; insurance card information; last calendar year's gross household income; and deductible expenses for the past year. The application is VA Form 10-10EZ.

question: What are the ways I can apply for VA health care?
ground_truth: Online, by phone, by mail, in person at a VA medical center or clinic, or with help from an accredited attorney, claims agent or Veterans Service Organization representative.

question: Where do I mail my VA health care application?
ground_truth: Health Eligibility Center, PO Box 5207, Janesville, WI 53547-5207.

question: How long does VA take to decide on my health care application?
ground_truth: Less than 1 week. If more than a week passes with no answer, do not apply again; call the toll-free hotline at 877-222-8387, Monday to Friday 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. ET.

question: Which form do I use to update my information after I already applied?
ground_truth: Use the Health Benefits Update Form (VA Form 10-10EZR).

question: Do I have to report my income when I apply?
ground_truth: No, you don't have to report income and expenses when you apply. But if you are not eligible based on other factors, VA will need that information to decide on your application.

question: I can't sign my form. What can I do?
ground_truth: If you sign with an X, two people you know must witness your signature and also sign and print their names on the form. You can also have someone acting as your power of attorney sign, with a copy of the power of attorney document.

question: How do I talk to someone right now in a crisis?
ground_truth: Veterans Crisis Line, free, confidential, 24/7: call 988 and press 1, start a chat, text 838255, or for TTY call 711 then 988. You can also call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room or VA medical center.

question: Do I need to be enrolled in VA health care to get mental health help?
ground_truth: No. You can get certain mental health services without enrollment by calling or walking in to any VA medical center or Vet Center.

question: Can I get mental health help online if I can't get to a VA facility?
ground_truth: Yes: the Veteran Training online self-help portal, VA mental health smartphone apps, and the VA telemental health program for video care from home.

question: What services do Vet Centers offer?
ground_truth: Individual and group counseling, couples and family counseling, military sexual trauma counseling, readjustment counseling, bereavement counseling, substance use assessment and referral, and help applying for VA benefits.

question: Can I talk to another Veteran who has been through this?
ground_truth: Yes. The BeThere peer assistance program with Military OneSource offers peer support at 800-342-9647, 24/7. You can also call 877-927-8387 to talk with a fellow combat Veteran.

question: What number do I call if I am a homeless Veteran?
ground_truth: National Call Center for Homeless Veterans: 877-424-3838, 24/7, free and confidential.

question: Which conditions does VA mental health care treat?
ground_truth: PTSD, depression, thoughts of suicide, military sexual trauma issues, substance use problems, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, and anxiety-related conditions such as generalized anxiety, panic disorder, social anxiety and phobias.
